names.kinzie_bake_house_1812: The Kinzie bake-house, behind the house's west end
names.kinzie_house_1812: The Kinzie house, built by Jean Baptiste Point du Sable

source.citation: "The Old Kinzie Mansion in 1832." — wood engraving, the upper panel of a plate with "Chicago in 1845, from the West", in George F. Cram, Cram's Standard American Railway System Atlas of the World / Columbian World's Fair Atlas (Chicago: George F. Cram, 1893).
what_it_does_not_supply: the house in 1812: it dates itself to 1832
what_it_supplies: the house long and low under a gable roof along the river, its west gable toward the eye
two stacks through the ridge, about 0.44 and 0.92 of it from the west gable
a piazza across the whole front, its roof drawn as the main roof carried down in one plane
a central door with two sash either side under the piazza
a picket fence round the green before the house, four columnar poplars in a row east of it, and a great tree behind
a two-storey house and a shed behind it to the north-west, in 1832
